stories.title: First Ever Recorded Sea Turtle Nests on America's West Coast
stories.label: ocean
stories.summary: For the first time ever, olive ridley sea turtles have laid their eggs on beaches in Southern California. Scientists were stunned to discover the nests, since these turtles have never been recorded building nests anywhere on the U.S. West Coast before. It's a rare and exciting milestone for marine biologists who study these threatened creatures. Researchers are now monitoring the nests closely, hopeful that healthy hatchlings will soon make their way to the sea. It's a small sign that ocean habitats along the coast may be shifting in the turtles' favor.
stories.why_good: A real, documented first-of-its-kind wildlife event that expands where an endangered species is thriving.

stories.title: Coastal Golf Course Turned into Vital Wetland Habitat for Seabirds
stories.label: earth
stories.summary: A golf course along England's coast has been turned into a brand-new wetland nature reserve. Even before it officially opened, plovers, terns, avocets, and lapwings had already moved in to nest and feed there. It's a lovely example of reclaiming developed land and handing it back to nature. The birds clearly didn't wait for an invitation — they just showed up and settled in.
stories.why_good: Real, completed habitat restoration that is already benefiting wild seabird populations, with no political angle.

stories.title: New Gobi Desert Fossil Rewrites a Chapter of Mammal Evolution
stories.label: science
stories.summary: Scientists found a beautifully preserved fossil in Mongolia's Gobi Desert that's changing what we know about early mammals living alongside dinosaurs. The little creature, just described in the journal Nature, turns out to belong to a totally different family tree than researchers had long assumed. It's a reminder that our understanding of ancient life is still being rewritten, one careful discovery at a time. No plans or predictions here, just real scientists examining a real fossil and finding something surprising. It's the kind of quiet scientific win that expands human knowledge a little more.
stories.why_good: A genuine scientific discovery that actually happened, peer-reviewed and published, expanding our understanding of life's history without any suffering or controversy attached.
